what: The correct option's explanation gives the wrong error code. Moving a String out of `args[1]` inside `build(args: &[String])` is E0508 ("cannot move out of type `[String]`, a non-copy slice"), not E0507 "cannot move out of index". E0507 is what a Vec index gives; here `args` is a slice.
evidence: why: "Chapter 9: the shelf owns its books, so let query = args[1]; would be E0507, \"cannot move out of index\"." A scratch build of `fn build(args: &[String]) -> String { let query = args[1]; query }` on Rust 1.99.1 (edition 2024) printed: error[E0508]: cannot move out of type `[String]`, a non-copy slice ... move occurs because `args[_]` has type `String` ... help: consider cloning the value ... `args[1].clone()`.
fix: Change the text to: would be E0508, "cannot move out of type `[String]`, a non-copy slice" (and its help suggests `.clone()`). Better still, capture this as a small program so the claim is backed by a run.

what: The page says the fix is in the Compiler's last help, but that suggestion (`let words: &str = *"owl";`) doesn't compile. It is E0308, because `*"owl"` is still a `str`. A beginner who follows it gets a new error.
evidence: unsized.rs stderr: "help: consider borrowing here | 2 | let words: &str = *\"owl\";". Page: "The fix is in the last help: borrow it." A scratch build of exactly that line on 1.99.1 gave: error[E0308]: mismatched types ... expected `&str`, found `str` ... help: consider removing deref here.
fix: "The last help points the right way (borrow it), but taken literally it still fails: also remove the *, giving let words: &str = \"owl\";. Compiler suggestions are hints, not guarantees." That's a good detective moment.

what: Copy is described as 'only for small values'. Size isn't the rule: any type whose fields are all Copy and which has no Drop can be Copy, e.g. `[u8; 4096]` or a large struct of numbers. The real condition, stated elsewhere on the page, is no heap ownership and no destructor.
evidence: Panel 7: "Only for small values that live entirely on the plate". Recap: "Copy copies by itself, only for small plain values". Words: "for small values with no heap data".
fix: Replace "small" with "plain": "only for values whose every part is plain bytes on the plate (numbers, chars, bools and structs of those), with no heap data and no Drop. Usually small, but size isn't the rule."
